alt.en: A printed page of music, page 40, headed "XXXV. Bully in the Alley.", with four systems, each a voice part above a two-stave piano part, in 4/4. The voice part is marked "Solo." and "Chorus." in turn, with the words "So help my bob I'm bul-ly in the al-ley; Way... ay... bul-ly in the al-ley," and "Bul-ly down in our al-ley" under the notes. Small arrowheads stand over each "Way" and the "bul-" after it.
alt.es: Página impresa de música, página 40, con el encabezado "XXXV. Bully in the Alley.", con cuatro sistemas, cada uno con una voz sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas, en 4/4. La voz está marcada "Solo." y "Chorus.", alternando, con las palabras "So help my bob I'm bul-ly in the al-ley; Way... ay... bul-ly in the al-ley," y "Bul-ly down in our al-ley" bajo las notas. Sobre cada "Way" y el "bul-" que lo sigue hay pequeñas puntas de flecha.

caption.en: Bully in the Alley as No. XXXV of Cecil Sharp's English Folk-Chanteys (London, 1914), page 40, as John Short of Watchet sang it: the earliest known printing, the page our arrangement is read from, with arrowheads over the two pulls in each answer.
caption.es: Bully in the Alley como n.º XXXV de English Folk-Chanteys de Cecil Sharp (Londres, 1914), página 40, tal como la cantaba John Short, de Watchet: la impresión más antigua que se conoce, la página de la que se lee nuestro arreglo, con puntas de flecha sobre los dos tirones de cada respuesta.

source: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Chanteys, with pianoforte accompaniment, introduction and notes (London: Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co. and Schott & Co.; Taunton: Barnicott & Pearce, 1914), No. XXXV, "Bully in the Alley", p. 40

alt.en: Three printed lines from an old dictionary: "Bob, a shilling. Formerly bobstick, which may have been the original. Bob-a-nob, a shilling a-head." and "Bob, "s'help me bob," a street oath, equivalent to "so help me God.""
alt.es: Tres líneas impresas de un diccionario antiguo: "Bob, a shilling. Formerly bobstick, which may have been the original. Bob-a-nob, a shilling a-head." y "Bob, "s'help me bob," a street oath, equivalent to "so help me God.""

caption.en: "S'help me bob" in John Camden Hotten's Slang Dictionary (London, 1874), page 89: a street oath standing in for "so help me God", the oath behind the shantyman's "So help my bob".
caption.es: "S'help me bob" en The Slang Dictionary de John Camden Hotten (Londres, 1874), página 89: un juramento callejero en lugar de "so help me God" (que Dios me ayude), el juramento que hay detrás del "So help my bob" del shantyman.

source: John Camden Hotten, The Slang Dictionary: Etymological, Historical, and Anecdotal (London: Chatto and Windus, 1874), entries "Bob", p. 89 (detail)

alt.en: The top of a printed page of music: one system, a voice part above a two-stave piano part, marked "Solo." and "Chorus.", with the words "Bul-ly in Tin-pot al-ley; Way... ay... bul-ly in the al-ley." ending in a double bar. Below, the heading "Bully in the Alley." and two numbered lines: "2. Have you seen our Sally?" and "3. She's the girl in the alley."
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página impresa de música: un sistema, con una voz sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas, marcado "Solo." y "Chorus.", con las palabras "Bul-ly in Tin-pot al-ley; Way... ay... bul-ly in the al-ley." y una doble barra final. Debajo, el encabezado "Bully in the Alley." y dos versos numerados: "2. Have you seen our Sally?" y "3. She's the girl in the alley."

caption.en: The end of the tune on page 41 of Sharp's English Folk-Chanteys (1914), with the only other words he printed, lines 2 and 3: "Have you seen our Sally?" and "She's the girl in the alley.", which begin our verses 2 and 3.
caption.es: El final de la melodía en la página 41 de English Folk-Chanteys de Sharp (1914), con las únicas otras palabras que imprimió, los versos 2 y 3: "Have you seen our Sally?" y "She's the girl in the alley.", que abren nuestras estrofas 2 y 3.
